coupling: The first commit changes auto-sized A8 images to use a tight row stride and exact backing allocation. That is memory-safe by itself. The later commit clears each row through the next four-byte boundary, which is safe with the original padded stride but writes past the tight allocation when the two commits are combined. A correct fix must either preserve the stride/allocation invariant consumed by the later tail clear or bound that clear to the actual row stride; reverting either commit alone leaves the other change valid and does not expose the overflow.
